cards.question: What happens to spawned threads when main ends?
cards.answer: When the main thread is terminated, all threads forked or spawned from it are cleaned up, whether they have finished executing or not.

cards.question: What does JoinHandle::join return?
cards.answer: A std::thread::Result: Err if the thread panicked, or Ok<T> with the thread's return value. Unwrapping an Err panics the joining thread too.

cards.question: Why can scoped threads borrow locals?
cards.answer: std::thread::scope joins every spawned thread before the scope exits, so borrowed data outlives those threads.

cards.question: Why is Rc not Send or Sync?
cards.answer: Its counter updates are not atomic. If two threads increment or decrement at once, the count becomes inconsistent.

cards.question: What does Arc add over Rc?
cards.answer: Increment and decrement are atomic, so no two threads can mutate the count at the same time. That lets the pointer be shared and sent across threads.

cards.question: How does Mutex differ from RefCell on conflict?
cards.answer: RefCell panics on a conflicting borrow. Mutex or RwLock put the waiter to sleep and wake it when the lock is dropped.

cards.question: What is the difference between Send and Sync?
cards.answer: T is Send if ownership can move to another thread. T is Sync if &T is Send. Arc is Send; Rc is not. i32 is Sync; Cell<i32> is not.

cards.question: What does Condvar::wait do with the MutexGuard?
cards.answer: It unlocks the mutex and sleeps. When notified, it re-locks the mutex and returns the guard. Use notify_one or notify_all to wake waiters.
